title: Greystone Capital - Inference security & hosting discovery
next_steps: Send SOC 2 Type II report and ISO scope doc to Aisha
Provision 7-day dedicated cluster pilot and test prompts/throughput
Schedule follow-up technical deep dive with Aisha about KMS/HSM integration (tentative Apr 1)
Provide cost per 1k tokens comparison for hosted vs dedicated
action_items: Maya: Email SOC2 + ISO summary and link to security docs (due 2027-03-16)
Connor: Prepare pilot runbook and sample benchmark sheet (due 2027-03-18)
Aisha: Share Greystone PII/data retention policy and list of internal compliance stakeholders (due 2027-03-19)
Jordan: Send procurement timeline and contract contact details (due 2027-03-20)
summary: Initial security and deployment intake for inference platform selection. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for regulated trading models and client data. Main topics: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML + SSO provisioning, RBAC and least-privilege, KMS/HSM integration and bring-your-own-key, audit logs and retention, data residency and retention windows, and a proposed dedicated pilot to validate latency and throughput.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Torres: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, we can run about 50 minutes, is that still good?
[00:04] Samuel Price: Yeah that works, thanks Maya.
[00:08] Connor Liu: Hey, Connor from Redwood, I'll be the technical... I'm the SE.
[00:12] Aisha Khan: Aisha here, security architect, I'll lead the compliance questions.
[00:18] Liam O'Rourke: Liam, CTO, quick context — we're considering offloading inference for several trading models, lots of PII-ish customer metadata attached.
[00:28] Maya Torres: Great, quick agenda: 1) understand existing stack and constraints, 2) compliance gates (SOC2/ISO), 3) hosting options and KMS, 4) next steps.
[00:36] Priya Mehta: We're on AWS, C4 and EKS for most services.
[00:40] Connor Liu: Cool, makes sense. Do you currently run any models in-house or are you mostly using APIs?
[00:46] Samuel Price: We've got a mix — some internal models on P3s and a small Kubernetes inference fleet. We're looking for better throughput and cost predictability, plus proper auditability.
[00:54] Aisha Khan: First question: do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence? We need to map controls.
[00:59] Maya Torres: Yes, Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II. We also have an ISO 27001 scope doc for our control plane — I'll send the reports after the call.
[01:06] Aisha Khan: When you say "send the reports" — we need the actual attestations and the control matrix mapping to our control identifiers.
[01:12] Maya Torres: Understood, we'll attach the attestation PDF and a control mapping spreadsheet.
[01:16] Liam O'Rourke: For private deployments — can we run the control plane in our VPC?
[01:20] Connor Liu: We offer a private deployment option where the control plane connects to customer-managed networking. For the on-prem package we can hand over the control plane or run a SaaS control plane with VPN peering depending on your needs.
[01:29] Aisha Khan: KMS — do you support BYOK and HSM-backed keys? Our policy requires keys never leave our HSM.
[01:34] Connor Liu: Yes, we support BYOK via AWS KMS imports or external HSMs through an HSM gateway. For hosted we can accept a customer-managed KMS and perform envelope encryption so the master key stays in your account.
[01:43] Priya Mehta: How about tokenization and PII redaction?
[01:46] Maya Torres: We have prefix caching and automatic KV cache — sorry, bad word, KV cash in the transcript — but in practice we have tools to avoid storing PII in logs and configurable redaction at the ingress.
[01:55] Samuel Price: Auditability: we need immutable audit logs, SIEM integration, and retention for 7 years for some workflows.
[02:02] Connor Liu: Our audit logs are append-only, we can stream logs to your S3 or to a SIEM via syslog/HTTP. Retention is configurable; for long-term storage we recommend offloading to your account S3 with lifecycle policies.
[02:12] Aisha Khan: Can we get raw request/response logs for a sample period? We need to run a compliance analysis.
[02:17] Connor Liu: We can enable request-level logging for the pilot and send a sanitized sample. For production we advise token-level redaction unless you have contractual need.
[02:27] Liam O'Rourke: Data residency: most of our EU clients require EU-only processing. How does Redwood handle regional routing and model pinning?
[02:33] Maya Torres: We have regional routing policies; you can pin workloads to a region or to a Dedicated pool running in eu-west-1. We also offer private deployments inside your network if you need full residency.
[02:43] Samuel Price: Latency is important — trading signals are time sensitive. What's typical p95 for hosted vs dedicated?
[02:49] Connor Liu: Hosted depends on model and seq length; for our small LLMs p95 can be sub 100ms for short prompts in hosted, but for heavier models we recommend Dedicated where the p95 is more predictable around 80-200ms depending on GPUs and batching. We'll provide benchmark sheets.
[03:03] Aisha Khan: SSO and provisioning — we use Okta. We need SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for groups and RBAC sync.
[03:10] Maya Torres: We support SAML and SCIM. You can map Okta groups to Redwood roles and we support role-based access with fine-grained admin vs viewer separation.
[03:18] Priya Mehta: Do you have support for service accounts and least privilege for application calls?
[03:22] Connor Liu: Yes, tokens can be scoped per-route and per-model. We recommend issuing short-lived service tokens and rotating them. For private deployments you can also configure network-level service accounts.
[03:31] Samuel Price: For regulators, audit trails of policy changes are big — RBAC changes, who rolled out model versions, rollbacks — can we see that?
[03:37] Connor Liu: All admin events are logged with actor, timestamp, and change. We can send those audit streams to your SIEM or S3.
[03:44] Aisha Khan: Encryption at rest — are embeddings and cached KV encrypted with customer keys?
[03:49] Connor Liu: Yes, data at rest is encrypted. For Hosted we support envelope encryption with customer-managed keys. For Dedicated and Private you'd typically run keys in your KMS/HSM.
[03:58] Maya Torres: Quick clarify — sometimes our docs say "we encrypt at rest and in transit" but the real ask is cryptographic separation of logs and model weights, so we can produce a control mapping.
[04:06] Aisha Khan: Exactly. Also need to know where any customer-derived artifacts (cached prefixes, fine-tuned artifacts) live and retention delete flows.
[04:13] Connor Liu: Cached prefixes and fine-tune artifacts can be configured to store in your account S3 in private deployments; in hosted they live in our encrypted storage but we can set TTLs and purge hooks. We'll include retention API docs.
[04:24] Samuel Price: About pricing: if we go Dedicated, are there long-term commits and burst capacity?
[04:29] Maya Torres: Dedicated is commit-based with optional burst pools. We can size the pilot at a lower commit to prove perf and then recommend a commit band.
[04:36] Liam O'Rourke: Pilot: we want a 7-day pilot with our trading prompts, full logging, and KMS BYOK — can you do that?
[04:42] Connor Liu: Yes, we can stand up a constrained Dedicated cluster for 7 days and enable request logging and your KMS integration. We'll need IP allowlist and Okta SAML config from Aisha.
[04:51] Aisha Khan: We'll share SAML metadata and the KMS contact. Also need an NDA addendum around sample logs.
[04:58] Jordan Vale: Procurement — typical lead time for a pilot contract? We budget 2 weeks for legal review.
[05:03] Maya Torres: We usually have a pilot MSA template, we can push a redline-friendly version. Two weeks is workable.
[05:09] Connor Liu: Quick technical question from me — what are your sequence lengths and qps expectations?
[05:13] Priya Mehta: Typical prompts are 512 tokens, with occasional bursts to 2048. Avg qps around 8 with spikes to 60 during market opens.
[05:22] Connor Liu: Great, that'll inform batch sizing and kernel selection; we'll run those workload sims in the benchmark.
[05:28] Aisha Khan: Back to controls — do you offer penetration test results or red team summary?
[05:33] Maya Torres: We have a pen test summary and remediation tracker; we can share redacted reports.
[05:39] Samuel Price: What about breach notification SLAs?
[05:43] Maya Torres: Incident response: we have a 72-hour notification window and can escalate per contract to 24 hours for higher tiers.
[05:50] Liam O'Rourke: Are there export controls or data egress notes we should be aware of when crossing regions?
[05:56] Connor Liu: We support region restrictions and can disable cross-region fallback; but do flag that some model backends in hosted may not be available in every region — we'll validate availability for eu-west-1 and us-east-1.
[06:06] Aisha Khan: For the SOC2 mapping, what's your change management control — do you have documented runbooks and staging audits?
[06:11] Maya Torres: Yes, we have documented change control, PR-based deploys, and can share the control owner list and runbook snippets.
[06:18] Priya Mehta: Any concerns about data being used to improve models? Our contracts require no training on customer data.
[06:23] Maya Torres: Redwood does not use customer data to train or improve models for hosted, per contract. We'll include contractual language to that effect.
[06:29] Samuel Price: Ok, sounds good. Can you put together a package: SOC2, ISO scope, pen test summary, pilot runbook, pilot cost estimate, and the dedicated cluster spec?
[06:37] Maya Torres: Yes, we'll package that and aim to get it out by Tuesday.
[06:40] Connor Liu: I'll also attach a short spreadsheet that maps your qps and seq lengths to expected latency and cost.
[06:46] Aisha Khan: Also need a sample of the audit log schema so our SIEM team can validate ingestion.
[06:52] Connor Liu: We'll include the JSON schema and a small sample set (sanitized).
[06:56] Jordan Vale: Procurement will expect a line-item pilot invoice.
[06:59] Maya Torres: We'll provide standard pilot invoice templates and options for PO or card.
[07:03] Maya Torres: Recap — Redwood to send SOC2/ISO and pen test, Connor to prepare pilot runbook and benchmark sheet, set up Dedicated 7-day pilot with KMS BYOK and Okta SAML if legal clears NDA addendum. Greystone to share SAML metadata, KMS contacts, and retention policy. Everyone agreed?
[07:18] Aisha Khan: Yes.
[07:20] Samuel Price: Yep.
[07:22] Liam O'Rourke: Thanks all.
[07:24] Maya Torres: Thanks, we'll follow up in email with attachments and next meeting invite.
[07:28] [meeting ended]
